key_highlights: ASX slides as banks and miners wobble; tech stocks resilient amid Wall Street AI sell-off
Oil spike from Houthi control of Hormuz choke point pressures airlines and fuels inflation concerns
AUD hit by Hormuz geopolitical risk; fuel price blowout pressures Albanese government on excise cut
Inflation persists across consumer staples (Maccas, electronics); mortgage stress and negative equity hit young Australians
Fed meeting in focus this week; retail sales data due
Mining sector mixed: coal demand resilient, gold exploration active (Forrestania, PLC Resources), tin-tungsten discovery (Critica 19Mt)
Major private hospital operator breakup signals healthcare sector consolidation
Australia nears energy inflection point; immigration policy debate intensifies

sectors.trend: Mixed. Coal demand resilient ('demise greatly exaggerated'), gold exploration active with Forrestania 2Mt WA deal and PLC Resources targeting bigger WA gold deposit. Critica's 19Mt tin-tungsten discovery in Tasmania is notable. Underground mine safety incident (pipe blast) raises operational risk. Steelworks job cuts signal structural weakness.
sectors.implications: Gold and critical minerals (tin, tungsten, graphite) offer diversification. Coal names (BHP.AX, BRL.AX) may outperform on demand resilience. Steel (BLT.AX) faces headwinds. Sarytogan's 97.7% battery-grade graphite yield supports EV supply chain plays.

sectors.trend: Banks wobbling on ASX. Mortgage stress and negative equity among young Australians signal rising NPL risk. Bank exits from truck financing for mid-size fleets indicate tightening credit. Fuel price pressure on household budgets may dampen lending demand.
sectors.implications: CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX face margin pressure from rate sensitivity and credit risk. Monitor NPL trends. REITs (VGP.AX, DGP.AX) under pressure from mortgage stress on tenant affordability.

sectors.trend: Oil spike from Houthi control of Hormuz choke point. Australia nears energy inflection point. Shipping giant installing 35m sail to cut fuel costs. Mongolian gas flows surging via TMK Energy. Fuel price blowout driving political pressure for excise cut.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) benefit from oil price support. Airlines (QAN.AX) face margin compression. Energy transition stocks gain narrative support. LNG exporters (BHP.AX, WDS.AX) supported by commodity prices.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator breakup after lenders back consortium bid signals sector consolidation. Amgen fell 5% on Lp(a) drug concerns. Bird flu in endangered sea lions raises biosecurity concerns.
sectors.implications: CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. Hospital operator breakup may create M&A opportunities. Monitor private health insurance (IAG.AX, MCF.AX) for cost pass-through.

sectors.trend: ASX tech shrugs off Wall Street AI sell-off. AI agents integrating with Visa/Mastercard payments. Nvidia redefining AI infrastructure as income asset. Trump vs tech chiefs on AI speed. Economic puzzle behind AI doomsday warnings.
sectors.implications: ASX tech (WES.AX, XRO.AX, SOL.AX) showing relative resilience. AI infrastructure spend supports long-term capex cycles. Payments disruption risk for financials.

sectors.trend: Inflation hitting Australians across Maccas meals and electronics. Fuel price blowout squeezing household budgets. Steakhouse chain closing 40+ locations. Coffeehouse Chapter 11 filing. Young homeowners accepting falling house prices.
sectors.implications: WES.AX, WOW.AX, CSG.AX face margin pressure from input costs. Value retail may outperform. Housing downturn (negative equity) weighs on construction (WBC.AX, GPT.AX).

key_themes: Geopolitical oil risk (Hormuz/Houthis) driving commodity volatility and AUD weakness
Persistent inflation eroding household purchasing power; fuel excise political pressure
Banking sector under stress from mortgage/NPL risks and credit tightening
Critical minerals and gold exploration pipeline strengthening (tin, tungsten, graphite, gold)
AI/tech resilience vs broader market weakness; payments disruption emerging
Energy transition inflection point in Australia
Immigration policy debate affecting labour supply and productivity narrative
Fed meeting and US retail sales as key near-term catalysts

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Hormuz Strait disruption / oil price spike
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge energy exposure; favour domestic LNG producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX) over import-dependent sectors. Monitor AUD/USD for carry trade unwinding.
Favour dividend-paying defensives (CSL.AX, WES.AX). Reduce exposure to rate-sensitive REITs and construction. Monitor RBA commentary.
Monitor NPL trends at CBA.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX, WBC.AX. Diversify away from concentrated bank exposure. Watch truck financing exits as leading indicator.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Fed policy uncertainty / US retail sales miss
risk_assessment.mitigation: Position for volatility around Fed decision. Maintain cash reserves. Monitor AUD/USD and global risk sentiment.
Monitor safety records at BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX. Pipe blast incident at underground mine warrants sector-wide safety review.

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Immigration policy shift affecting labour supply
risk_assessment.mitigation: Assess impact on construction, healthcare, and services sectors. Monitor productivity data. One Nation policy push may alter political landscape.

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold and critical minerals exploration names
opportunities.rationale: Forrestania 2Mt WA gold deal, PLC Resources gold target, Critica 19Mt tin-tungsten, Sarytogan graphite yield signal strong exploration pipeline. Geopolitical risk supports gold.

opportunities.recommendation: Add domestic energy producers on oil spike
opportunities.rationale: Hormuz disruption supports oil/LNG prices. WDS.AX and STO.AX benefit from higher realisations. Energy inflection point narrative supports structural demand.

opportunities.recommendation: Selective tech/AI exposure via ASX-listed names
opportunities.rationale: ASX tech resilient vs Wall Street sell-off. AI payments integration (Visa/Mastercard) and infrastructure spend support long-term thesis. XRO.AX, WES.AX offer diversification.

defensive_moves.rationale: Mortgage stress, negative equity, falling house prices, and tenant affordability pressure weigh on VGP.AX, DGP.AX, GPT.AX. Young homeowner distress signals demand softening.

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge AUD weakness and oil volatility
defensive_moves.rationale: Hormuz risk and Fed uncertainty create two-way AUD volatility. Maintain cash or short-duration bonds. Consider AUD put options.
Inflation squeezing household budgets. Steakhouse closures, coffeehouse bankruptcies signal demand destruction. WES.AX, WOW.AX, CSG.AX offer defensive income.

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure (1-3 months). Oil spike from Hormuz, Fed meeting uncertainty, and inflation persistence cap upside. Banks and miners wobble. Tech provides relative support. Expect elevated volatility. RBA on hold but hawkish bias likely given inflation stickiness. AUD vulnerable to risk-off flows.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive. Energy transition inflection, critical minerals pipeline, and AI infrastructure spend support structural themes. However, household debt stress, immigration policy uncertainty, and global growth deceleration cap re-rating potential. ASX 200 likely range-bound with sector rotation favouring energy, gold, and tech over banks and REITs.
